Hi Sarah —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have a shared starting point for the POC with Acme: 

Summary of needs:
- Real-time assistant for internal support agents (NLP routing + suggested replies)
- Latency target: 300ms p95 for token generation on average request sizes
- Accuracy bar: >= 85% on intent classification + acceptable F1 on entity extraction for top 10 intents
- Data handling: customer content must remain within our VPC for the POC

Proposed POC scope (2 weeks):
1) Integration: sample Slack/Helpdesk logs (anonymized) to validate routing accuracy
2) Offline eval: run ~500 labeled threads through eval rubric to measure accuracy & hallucination rate
3) Online shadow (optional): serve in shadow mode behind agents for 3 business days to gather latency and real-world failure modes
4) Success criteria: defined pass/fail on offline eval + latency requirements met in shadow run

Ownership suggestion: 
- Redwood SE (Marissa) owns integration + eval execution
- Acme data lead (Rajesh) provides anonymized logs and signs off on test data readiness

Next actions: 
- I attached a one-page POC plan and a draft evaluation rubric (Acme_POCPlan_v1.pdf, Redwood_eval_rubric.xlsx). Please confirm success criteria and whether you prefer offline-only evaluation or include a short online shadow.
- Suggest we kick off next Monday (6/22) if that works for your team — estimated 2-week calendar POC.

Thanks,
Dylan Brooks
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Hi all —

A couple of notes on evaluation methodology from the SE perspective: 

1) Offline vs online shadow: we usually recommend starting offline to ensure label-level quality and to iterate on prompt/template changes quickly. Offline eval gives faster signal on model selection and quantization options.
2) Rubric and grading: we'll run both aggregate metrics (accuracy, F1, hallucination rate) and example-level pass/fail with human adjudication for ~100 edge cases. The rubric spreadsheet includes sample thresholds — happy to adjust them to match Acme thresholds (we set intent >= 0.85, entities F1 >= 0.78 as suggested).
3) Data sampling: ask Rajesh for a stratified sample across priority queues (billing, technical, product). This avoids dataset skew.
4) Timeline: once data is uploaded (target 6/19), I expect offline eval results by EOD 6/23. If results are acceptable, shadow kickoff can be 6/24–6/26.

I'll start the eval run as soon as we have the dataset and will include an initial findings doc and a few example transcripts.

Cheers,
Marissa Cole
